articles.title: Liverpool look for new sporting director after Richard Hughes formally leaves
articles.summary: Hughes in line for similar role at Saudi club Al-Hilal. FSG president Mike Gordon leads search for successor. Liverpool are searching for a fourth sporting director in four years after confirming that Richard Hughes has stepped down from the role.
body: Hughes’s departure has been long expected, with the 47-year-old in line to take up a similar position with the Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal. He informed Liverpool of his intentions to leave early this year, after the departure of his friend Michael Edwards as chief executive of football for Fenway Sports Group, the club’s owner.

With work already under way on Liverpool’s summer transfer targets – including the signing of Bradley Barcola in a £123m deal – and Hughes enjoying a close working relationship with the new head coach, Andoni Iraola, it was agreed he would continue in the role until the end of the transfer window.
Liverpool say no approach was received from Al-Hilal for Hughes to start work with them this summer and are satisfied the sporting director worked for them alone throughout this period.

The search for Hughes’s replacement is already under way and is being led by FSG’s president, Mike Gordon, who resumed the day-to-day running of the club after Edwards’ exit. The eventual appointment will follow in the footsteps since Edwards left the role in 2022 of Julian Ward, Jörg Schmadtke and Hughes.

articles.title: CTE in football players is a health crisis. It’s time for us to stop watching
articles.summary: A new study offers more evidence that America’s biggest sport produces life-altering head trauma. The NFL will never turn itself off, so it’s on fans to do so. As a new NFL season begins this Wednesday, the danger of America’s most-watched sport has never been more clear.
body: A new and widely circulated study published in the British Journal of Medicine examined the donated brains of former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 and compared them with the overall number of players who died during that period. Of the 235 donated brains in that period, 215 had evidence of the degenerative brain condition chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE). That group of 215 comprised 24.5% of the former players who died during that period in total. Given the finding, the study’s authors estimate that the prevalence of CTE among players who died in that period was at minimum 24.5% to a maximum of 97.7%, with the actual rate likely somewhere in between.

Nathan Kalman-Lamb is Associate Professor of Sociology at the University of New Brunswick. Derek Silva is Associate Professor of Sociology and Criminology at King’s University College at Western University.

articles.title: FIA appeal court refutes Briatore impartiality claim
articles.summary: The FIA court of appeal refutes a claim by Alpine boss Flavio Briatore which it says "question the independence and impartiality of the judges".
body: Briatore claimed on Friday that one of the court of appeal judges in the case that ended with the court re-instating a penalty on Alpine's Pierre Gasly in the Monaco Grand Prix had "links" with McLaren.

The statement by the highest legal authority of motorsport's governing body said that court of appeal judges are "subject to the independence and confidentiality requirements contained in the FIA judicial and disciplinary rules, make annual disclosures of interests to the FIA compliance officer, and sign a specific declaration of independence for each particular case in consideration of the issue at stake and the parties involved".
It added that the parties to the dispute were invited both before and after the hearing "to raise any issues concerning the proceedings or the composition of the court. None did so".
It added: "No objection was raised during the hearing concerning the manner in which the court questioned the witness or conducted the proceedings.

articles.title: Sussex pick up crucial win at struggling Essex
articles.summary: Sussex all but secure their Division One status with a 47-run victory over Essex, who remain in relegation trouble.
body: Sussex took an hour and 20 minutes and 21 overs to wrap up the last three Essex wickets and complete a 47-run victory that lifts them clear of any lingering worries about relegation from Division One of the County Championship.

However, they met stern resistance from Essex all-rounder Matt Critchley who batted for three-and-a-half hours in defying Sussex's efforts. He was eventually last man out when he popped up a catch to slip off James Coles for 96 from 132 balls.
It was the third time this season Critchley, who has 838 Championship runs to his name, has been out in the nineties. His innings included two sixes and eight fours.

Shane Snater (35) had given Essex some hope, hitting two sixes himself in a 45-ball cameo that put on 48 for the ninth wicket, but it was merely brief entertainment for the sizeable crowd who had turned up in the hope of a miracle that did not happen.

articles.title: Manchester United and the 45 minutes that put them in the sights of the WSL’s chasing pack
articles.summary: “We cannot lose time,” Eva Olid told reporters, unpicking her Manchester United team’s season-opening defeat to London City Lionesses on Friday. “From minute one, we need to be ourselves.” Olid took over as head coach of United one month ago after the departure of Marc Skinner.
body: United, who finished fourth last season, were beaten 2-1 by an unrelenting and hungry London City side. Julia Zigiotti inadvertently headed into her own net under pressure from Alanna Kennedy on a corner kick in the ninth minute. Danielle van de Donk doubled their lead late in the second half with a flick after a poorly defended corner. Substitute Simi Awujo’s strike, the last move of the game, was too little, too late for United.
Two set pieces made the difference, but that belies the uncomfortable truth for United. The aim under Olid is possession-based, front-footed football. Instead, they were dominated.

“I always say that it’s a process,” Olid said. “In three weeks, I try (to make it so) that the team believes that we can be a team that dominates with the ball and attacks. And of course, I think it’s something more mental.
“In the first half, we could feel like the players were not believing in having the ball. And at half-time, I said to them: ‘Listen, this is not us. We need the ball to be ourselves’.”

articles.summary: Rich Eisen, the former SportsCenter anchor who now runs his own successful show, just put out a list of the biggest game-wreckers in the NFL. And Ja’Marr Chase was named the third-biggest game-wrecker, just ahead of receiver Puka Nacua of the Los Angeles Rams.
body: “Let’s not forget who this guy is, right? He is a game-wrecker. He’ll just collect receptions, and it’s like, how many times, when [Joe] Burrow finds him, when healthy, or Jake Browning did or [Joe] Flacco did, where it’s like, is anybody aware that Ja’Marr Chase is out on the field? Why is he open? Why is he getting free releases? Why? And then he’s gone. Then he just goes for 80 yards.”
Ahead of Chase on Eisen’s list were Buffalo Bills QB Josh Allen (second) and Rams pass rusher Myles Garrett (first).
We discussed that, while Chase is not declining at all, his stats might go down this year on account of a more conservative offense.

articles.title: Erasmus and Rennie's war of words escalates ahead of third Test
articles.summary: The four-match series is finely poised at 1-1, with Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry seemingly reaching new heights of tension as Rassie Erasmus and Dave Rennie’s war of words escalates.
body: Picture the scene: The touring All Blacks win the opening Test with a 33-16 at Ellis Park. Then, the Springboks hit back with a thrilling 33-26 victory over New Zealand in Cape Town.

Named in the front row for the Springboks for that contest were Ox Nche, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw. Just one hour before kick-off, that was changed to Gerhard Steenekamp, Deon Fourie and Thomas du Toit with the original three dropping to the bench.
Erasmus said this was down to conditions and a chance of rain not materialising.
"We thought it was going to be wet and that's why we picked the front row, Erasmus said after the match. "The whole weather prediction, the whole week, was it was going to be wet."

body: St Helens' standing at seventh on the Super League ladder for the 2026 season was confirmed on Friday night after they were thumped 48-10 by Leigh Leopards, while Hull KR's 36-6 win against Huddersfield confirmed the top six.
It was Saints' seventh defeat in their last 10 matches and second heavy loss in a row, having suffered a 28-point reverse to Leeds a week ago.

O'Carroll is due to be replaced by former Brisbane Broncos and Australia head coach Kevin Walters ahead of the 2027 season, and the experienced coach will hope to galvanise the Saints back to their best next season.
But eyebrows have been raised over the team's recruitment decisions this year, with the club also struggling with a big injury crisis. At one stage in July, 16 players were sidelined with injuries.
